title: Hymns of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
author: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints (editor, compiler)
edition_analyzed: 1985 English edition (commonly used in LDS congregations worldwide; later editions are minor reprints; new revision expected 2026)
target_audience: Members of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints (LDS, Mormon)
Those interested in modern Christian hymnals
core_themes: Worship and praise of God and Jesus Christ
Restoration of the gospel and prophetic revelation
primary_purpose: To provide a standardized collection of hymns for worship, doctrine instruction, and spiritual edification in individual, family, and congregational settings within the LDS Church.

structure_format.narrative_style: Non-narrative; a curated anthology of hymns and sacred songs with music notation
structure_format.organization: Divided into 341 numbered hymns, followed by indexes (alphabetical, topical, authors/composers, meters, scripture references, etc.)

key_concepts_lessons: Spirituality is deepened through sacred music in worship.
Hymns reinforce doctrine and religious values.
Singing together promotes unity and faith within congregations.
Music can be a form of prayer, testimony, and worship.
Many hymns reflect unique LDS teachings such as continuing revelation, modern prophets, and the Restoration.
notable_features: Blend of traditional Christian hymns and uniquely Latter-day Saint compositions
Content shaped by church leadership and member submissions
Widely used for nearly four decades as the standard English-language hymnal in LDS worship
Indices and supplemental information support liturgical planning and study
Forthcoming substantial update (expected 2026) to expand global inclusivity
cultural_historical_context: Commissioned in the late 1970s and published in 1985, this hymnal arose during a period of global growth in the LDS Church and reflected both preservation of historic Christian hymns and development of doctrinally distinctive LDS music. It succeeded the 1948 English-language edition, with careful attention to inclusivity, musical accessibility, and spiritual resonance for a worldwide church. The 1985 edition has defined worship music for several LDS generations.
reception_impact: Embraced as a central component of LDS worship and devotional life worldwide
Many hymns have become beloved standards and are sung at baptisms, funerals, weddings, and general conferences
Musical arrangements from the hymnal are widely used by choirs and instrumentalists
Some members have advocated for greater cultural and linguistic diversity, informing the ongoing revision process
comparable_titles: Songs of Zion (LDS black cultural supplement)
Children's Songbook (LDS Church; companion volume for children)
